children: Oil rises in early Asian trade. Oil prices are still expected to decline, but the path lower is likely to be more gradual as the endgame of the U.S.-Iran conflict becomes increasingly difficult to predict, OCBC Group Research strategists write in a note. Disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz, tighter U.S. sanctions on Iran, shrinking inventories, and constrained refining capacity are keeping a firm floor under crude and refined product prices, they add. Front-month WTI crude oil futures are up 1.1% at $93.42 a barrel, while Brent is 1.6% higher at $105.95 a barrel. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com)
